items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: On the 25th of November, I made my first recording in France with Garnet Clarke... Garnet played great piano on this recording.

ctx.x: I don't remember what the style of the pianist was like but Jerry played nice swinging drums and Django was great. I thought he was great because I could not speak French and he did not understand English. And I had never before played for such an enthusiastic crowd of people as those French jazz fans. The hall could hold about 300 people and it was almost if not full and our success was overwhelming.

On the 25th of November, I made my first recording in France with Garnet Clarke, George Johnson, Django Reinhardt, and June Cole the bass player of Willie Lewis's orchestra. June had played with the Cinco Septett that had later become the McKinney's Cotton Pickers and with Fletcher Henderson before joining Willie Lewis in Europe. And it was the first time that I sang a song solo on a record. The title was 'The Object of my Affection'. We had a fast tempo and I almost choked trying to sing the last four measures…

Garnet seemed to be a little deranged. When I recorded with him, I didn't know too much about him. Apparently, what had happened was that he had been down in the South of France, and all of a sudden he decided he wanted to come back to Paris. When he arrived there, he was going to stay at a certain hotel but he wanted first to see a lady friend of his. Unfortunately when they arrived, this lady was out, so he asked his taxi driver to drive around for a bit, but when they returned the lady was still not back. So…
